summary: A change notice for IMP system version 2513. The delay before a host just coming up may send messages through the IMP was lengthened, and IMPs gained the ability to test their host interfaces under Network Control Center control, to help locate faults.

plainLanguage.summary: The network box now makes a computer wait longer after it turns on, and it can test its own plug to find broken connections.

subtitle: Software changes to the ARPA Network IMP system

tldr.problem: The IMP system needs adjustments to host startup behavior and troubleshooting capabilities.
tldr.mechanism: IMP system version 2513 increases the startup delay before a host can send messages into the network from 30-60 seconds to 40 seconds to 1 minute 15 seconds, and adds the ability for the Network Control Center to test IMP host interfaces.
tldr.outcome: Better reliability during host startup and improved ability to diagnose host-to-IMP connection problems.

today: This was a system change notification from November 1971. The IMP software has long since been superseded by modern internet routing systems.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 256 announces a new version of the IMP system, version 2513, which was to be installed shortly on the ARPA Network. The version incorporates two principal changes affecting host startup and network troubleshooting.
sections.plainLanguage: The network is getting a software update with two improvements.

sections.title: Increased Host Startup Delay
sections.content: A host will now be prevented from sending any messages into the network for between 40 seconds and 1 minute 15 seconds after it comes alive. This is an increase from the previous limit of 30 seconds to 1 minute. The longer delay allows the host and IMP to stabilize their connection before network traffic begins.
sections.plainLanguage: When a computer turns on and connects to the network box, it must wait longer before it can send its first messages.

sections.title: IMP Host Interface Testing
sections.content: The IMP has been given the ability to test its host interface under control of the Network Control Center (NCC). This testing capability helps operators isolate problems when the communication path between the IMP and its host is faulty, reducing the time and effort needed to diagnose and repair connection issues.
sections.plainLanguage: The network box can now check if its cable to the computer is working properly, which helps find broken connections faster.
